summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes and a history of kidney transplantation was admitted with fever and pelvic pressure, concerning for recurrent urinary tract infection. She had recently completed a 14-day course of ertapenem for multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae. Given her history, she was started empirically on IV meropenem. Urine culture confirmed MDR Klebsiella, and she responded well, becoming afebrile within 24 hours. Renal ultrasound showed stable transplant anatomy with no obstruction. Her creatinine, initially elevated to 1.3, improved to 1.0 with IV fluids. Due to persistent infection risk, she was transitioned to outpatient IV ertapenem for a total 21-day course via a midline. Estring was initiated to reduce future UTI risk, and she was advised to resume weekly fosfomycin after completing antibiotics. Her insulin pump was re-sited after transient hyperglycemia, and she was discharged home with visiting nurse services and follow-up plans.
